payload.objective: Repair the existing interval-window aggregation defect by implementing one deterministic algorithm in src/windows.js while preserving the existing InvalidWindowError RangeError contract and leaving all tests and dependencies unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Only src/windows.js is modified; no tests are changed, deleted, skipped, or weakened, and no dependency is added.
Every input window is validated before aggregation; malformed windows are converted to InvalidWindowError, which remains a RangeError with code INVALID_WINDOW.
Input is sorted through a copied representation so caller-owned window order and window objects are not mutated.
Windows merge only when their overlap has positive width; an end equal to the next start remains a separate boundary.
Merged labels are unique strings sorted in lexicographic order.
The real project checker is run as npm test, whose underlying command is node --test, and all tests pass.
payload.root_design_decision: Use a validate-then-copy-sort-then-sweep pipeline: validate every window and its start/end/labels shape before any result is produced; sort copied window records by deterministic interval order; sweep from left to right, merging only when next.start is strictly less than the current end, extending the current end as needed, and accumulating labels in a Set before final lexicographic sorting. Equality at the boundary is deliberately non-overlapping.
owned_modification_surfaces: src/windows.js: InvalidWindowError contract preservation, window validation, copied deterministic ordering, positive-width overlap sweep, and unique lexicographic label aggregation.
ordered_implementation_work: Inspect the existing src/windows.js exports and data shape without changing tests or package configuration.

Implement a validation predicate for every window consistent with the observed start/end/labels object shape; route all malformed cases through InvalidWindowError and preserve RangeError plus code INVALID_WINDOW.
Create a shallow copied working collection (and copied label arrays/records where needed), then sort it deterministically without mutating caller input.

Implement the sweep: start a new output interval when there is no positive-width overlap; merge only when next.start < current.end; keep next.start === current.end separate; extend end to the maximum endpoint.
Finalize each output interval with deduplicated labels sorted by standard lexicographic string ordering, preserving the expected output shape and named exports.
Run npm test through the real project checker and confirm the underlying node --test suite passes; report the exact result.
positive_non_user_interface_verification: Run npm test from the project root (the package script invokes node --test).
Confirm all existing tests pass, including overlap merge, adjacent-boundary separation, and InvalidWindowError RangeError/code assertions.
If implementation-time checks are needed, use only existing project tooling and do not add dependencies or alter tests.
payload.required_real_page_visual_acceptance: Not applicable: this is a non-UI algorithm repair with no page, component, or visual surface.
risks: The research report notes that the visible files do not fully specify finite versus integer endpoint requirements, zero-width validity, or whether empty labels are allowed; validation must follow the established src/windows.js contract and test expectations rather than inventing incompatible restrictions.
Lexicographic ordering must use the project/runtime's ordinary string comparison consistently, and sorting must not mutate caller-owned arrays.
unknowns: Exact malformed-window predicate beyond required start/end/labels fields is not fully specified by the research report.
Whether zero-width windows are valid inputs versus merely non-overlapping intervals is not established by the visible evidence.
Whether empty label arrays or empty label strings are valid is not established by the visible evidence.
blockers: No implementation blocker for planning. The Developer must resolve the noted validation edge semantics from the existing src/windows.js contract and tests while preserving the explicit user requirements.

payload.objective: Repair the existing interval-window aggregation defect by implementing one deterministic algorithm in src/windows.js while preserving the existing InvalidWindowError RangeError contract and leaving all tests and dependencies unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Only src/windows.js is modified; no tests are changed, deleted, skipped, or weakened, and no dependency is added.
Every input window is validated before aggregation; malformed windows are converted to InvalidWindowError, which remains a RangeError with code INVALID_WINDOW.
Input is sorted through a copied representation so caller-owned window order and window objects are not mutated.
Windows merge only when their overlap has positive width; an end equal to the next start remains a separate boundary.
Merged labels are unique strings sorted in lexicographic order.
The real project checker is run as npm test, whose underlying command is node --test, and all tests pass.
payload.root_design_decision: Use a validate-then-copy-sort-then-sweep pipeline: validate every window and its start/end/labels shape before any result is produced; sort copied window records by deterministic interval order; sweep from left to right, merging only when next.start is strictly less than the current end, extending the current end as needed, and accumulating labels in a Set before final lexicographic sorting. Equality at the boundary is deliberately non-overlapping.
owned_modification_surfaces: src/windows.js: InvalidWindowError contract preservation, window validation, copied deterministic ordering, positive-width overlap sweep, and unique lexicographic label aggregation.
ordered_implementation_work: Inspect the existing src/windows.js exports and data shape without changing tests or package configuration.

Implement a validation predicate for every window consistent with the observed start/end/labels object shape; route all malformed cases through InvalidWindowError and preserve RangeError plus code INVALID_WINDOW.
Create a shallow copied working collection (and copied label arrays/records where needed), then sort it deterministically without mutating caller input.

Implement the sweep: start a new output interval when there is no positive-width overlap; merge only when next.start < current.end; keep next.start === current.end separate; extend end to the maximum endpoint.
Finalize each output interval with deduplicated labels sorted by standard lexicographic string ordering, preserving the expected output shape and named exports.
Run npm test through the real project checker and confirm the underlying node --test suite passes; report the exact result.
positive_non_user_interface_verification: Run npm test from the project root (the package script invokes node --test).
Confirm all existing tests pass, including overlap merge, adjacent-boundary separation, and InvalidWindowError RangeError/code assertions.
If implementation-time checks are needed, use only existing project tooling and do not add dependencies or alter tests.
payload.required_real_page_visual_acceptance: Not applicable: this is a non-UI algorithm repair with no page, component, or visual surface.
risks: The research report notes that the visible files do not fully specify finite versus integer endpoint requirements, zero-width validity, or whether empty labels are allowed; validation must follow the established src/windows.js contract and test expectations rather than inventing incompatible restrictions.
Lexicographic ordering must use the project/runtime's ordinary string comparison consistently, and sorting must not mutate caller-owned arrays.
unknowns: Exact malformed-window predicate beyond required start/end/labels fields is not fully specified by the research report.
Whether zero-width windows are valid inputs versus merely non-overlapping intervals is not established by the visible evidence.
Whether empty label arrays or empty label strings are valid is not established by the visible evidence.
blockers: No implementation blocker for planning. The Developer must resolve the noted validation edge semantics from the existing src/windows.js contract and tests while preserving the explicit user requirements.

payload.objective: Repair the existing interval-window aggregation defect by implementing one deterministic algorithm in src/windows.js while preserving the existing InvalidWindowError RangeError contract and leaving all tests and dependencies unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Only src/windows.js is modified; no tests are changed, deleted, skipped, or weakened, and no dependency is added.
Every input window is validated before aggregation; malformed windows are converted to InvalidWindowError, which remains a RangeError with code INVALID_WINDOW.
Input is sorted through a copied representation so caller-owned window order and window objects are not mutated.
Windows merge only when their overlap has positive width; an end equal to the next start remains a separate boundary.
Merged labels are unique strings sorted in lexicographic order.
The real project checker is run as npm test, whose underlying command is node --test, and all tests pass.
payload.root_design_decision: Use a validate-then-copy-sort-then-sweep pipeline: validate every window and its start/end/labels shape before any result is produced; sort copied window records by deterministic interval order; sweep from left to right, merging only when next.start is strictly less than the current end, extending the current end as needed, and accumulating labels in a Set before final lexicographic sorting. Equality at the boundary is deliberately non-overlapping.
owned_modification_surfaces: src/windows.js: InvalidWindowError contract preservation, window validation, copied deterministic ordering, positive-width overlap sweep, and unique lexicographic label aggregation.
ordered_implementation_work: Inspect the existing src/windows.js exports and data shape without changing tests or package configuration.

Implement a validation predicate for every window consistent with the observed start/end/labels object shape; route all malformed cases through InvalidWindowError and preserve RangeError plus code INVALID_WINDOW.
Create a shallow copied working collection (and copied label arrays/records where needed), then sort it deterministically without mutating caller input.

Implement the sweep: start a new output interval when there is no positive-width overlap; merge only when next.start < current.end; keep next.start === current.end separate; extend end to the maximum endpoint.
Finalize each output interval with deduplicated labels sorted by standard lexicographic string ordering, preserving the expected output shape and named exports.
Run npm test through the real project checker and confirm the underlying node --test suite passes; report the exact result.
positive_non_user_interface_verification: Run npm test from the project root (the package script invokes node --test).
Confirm all existing tests pass, including overlap merge, adjacent-boundary separation, and InvalidWindowError RangeError/code assertions.
If implementation-time checks are needed, use only existing project tooling and do not add dependencies or alter tests.
payload.required_real_page_visual_acceptance: Not applicable: this is a non-UI algorithm repair with no page, component, or visual surface.
risks: The research report notes that the visible files do not fully specify finite versus integer endpoint requirements, zero-width validity, or whether empty labels are allowed; validation must follow the established src/windows.js contract and test expectations rather than inventing incompatible restrictions.
Lexicographic ordering must use the project/runtime's ordinary string comparison consistently, and sorting must not mutate caller-owned arrays.
unknowns: Exact malformed-window predicate beyond required start/end/labels fields is not fully specified by the research report.
Whether zero-width windows are valid inputs versus merely non-overlapping intervals is not established by the visible evidence.
Whether empty label arrays or empty label strings are valid is not established by the visible evidence.
blockers: No implementation blocker for planning. The Developer must resolve the noted validation edge semantics from the existing src/windows.js contract and tests while preserving the explicit user requirements.

payload.objective: Repair the existing interval-window aggregation defect by implementing one deterministic algorithm in src/windows.js while preserving the existing InvalidWindowError RangeError contract and leaving all tests and dependencies unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Only src/windows.js is modified; no tests are changed, deleted, skipped, or weakened, and no dependency is added.
Every input window is validated before aggregation; malformed windows are converted to InvalidWindowError, which remains a RangeError with code INVALID_WINDOW.
Input is sorted through a copied representation so caller-owned window order and window objects are not mutated.
Windows merge only when their overlap has positive width; an end equal to the next start remains a separate boundary.
Merged labels are unique strings sorted in lexicographic order.
The real project checker is run as npm test, whose underlying command is node --test, and all tests pass.
payload.root_design_decision: Use a validate-then-copy-sort-then-sweep pipeline: validate every window and its start/end/labels shape before any result is produced; sort copied window records by deterministic interval order; sweep from left to right, merging only when next.start is strictly less than the current end, extending the current end as needed, and accumulating labels in a Set before final lexicographic sorting. Equality at the boundary is deliberately non-overlapping.
owned_modification_surfaces: src/windows.js: InvalidWindowError contract preservation, window validation, copied deterministic ordering, positive-width overlap sweep, and unique lexicographic label aggregation.
ordered_implementation_work: Inspect the existing src/windows.js exports and data shape without changing tests or package configuration.

Implement a validation predicate for every window consistent with the observed start/end/labels object shape; route all malformed cases through InvalidWindowError and preserve RangeError plus code INVALID_WINDOW.
Create a shallow copied working collection (and copied label arrays/records where needed), then sort it deterministically without mutating caller input.

Implement the sweep: start a new output interval when there is no positive-width overlap; merge only when next.start < current.end; keep next.start === current.end separate; extend end to the maximum endpoint.
Finalize each output interval with deduplicated labels sorted by standard lexicographic string ordering, preserving the expected output shape and named exports.
Run npm test through the real project checker and confirm the underlying node --test suite passes; report the exact result.
positive_non_user_interface_verification: Run npm test from the project root (the package script invokes node --test).
Confirm all existing tests pass, including overlap merge, adjacent-boundary separation, and InvalidWindowError RangeError/code assertions.
If implementation-time checks are needed, use only existing project tooling and do not add dependencies or alter tests.
payload.required_real_page_visual_acceptance: Not applicable: this is a non-UI algorithm repair with no page, component, or visual surface.
risks: The research report notes that the visible files do not fully specify finite versus integer endpoint requirements, zero-width validity, or whether empty labels are allowed; validation must follow the established src/windows.js contract and test expectations rather than inventing incompatible restrictions.
Lexicographic ordering must use the project/runtime's ordinary string comparison consistently, and sorting must not mutate caller-owned arrays.
unknowns: Exact malformed-window predicate beyond required start/end/labels fields is not fully specified by the research report.
Whether zero-width windows are valid inputs versus merely non-overlapping intervals is not established by the visible evidence.
Whether empty label arrays or empty label strings are valid is not established by the visible evidence.
blockers: No implementation blocker for planning. The Developer must resolve the noted validation edge semantics from the existing src/windows.js contract and tests while preserving the explicit user requirements.

payload.objective: Repair the existing interval-window aggregation defect by implementing one deterministic algorithm in src/windows.js while preserving the existing InvalidWindowError RangeError contract and leaving all tests and dependencies unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Only src/windows.js is modified; no tests are changed, deleted, skipped, or weakened, and no dependency is added.
Every input window is validated before aggregation; malformed windows are converted to InvalidWindowError, which remains a RangeError with code INVALID_WINDOW.
Input is sorted through a copied representation so caller-owned window order and window objects are not mutated.
Windows merge only when their overlap has positive width; an end equal to the next start remains a separate boundary.
Merged labels are unique strings sorted in lexicographic order.
The real project checker is run as npm test, whose underlying command is node --test, and all tests pass.
payload.root_design_decision: Use a validate-then-copy-sort-then-sweep pipeline: validate every window and its start/end/labels shape before any result is produced; sort copied window records by deterministic interval order; sweep from left to right, merging only when next.start is strictly less than the current end, extending the current end as needed, and accumulating labels in a Set before final lexicographic sorting. Equality at the boundary is deliberately non-overlapping.
owned_modification_surfaces: src/windows.js: InvalidWindowError contract preservation, window validation, copied deterministic ordering, positive-width overlap sweep, and unique lexicographic label aggregation.
ordered_implementation_work: Inspect the existing src/windows.js exports and data shape without changing tests or package configuration.

Implement a validation predicate for every window consistent with the observed start/end/labels object shape; route all malformed cases through InvalidWindowError and preserve RangeError plus code INVALID_WINDOW.
Create a shallow copied working collection (and copied label arrays/records where needed), then sort it deterministically without mutating caller input.

Implement the sweep: start a new output interval when there is no positive-width overlap; merge only when next.start < current.end; keep next.start === current.end separate; extend end to the maximum endpoint.
Finalize each output interval with deduplicated labels sorted by standard lexicographic string ordering, preserving the expected output shape and named exports.
Run npm test through the real project checker and confirm the underlying node --test suite passes; report the exact result.
positive_non_user_interface_verification: Run npm test from the project root (the package script invokes node --test).
Confirm all existing tests pass, including overlap merge, adjacent-boundary separation, and InvalidWindowError RangeError/code assertions.
If implementation-time checks are needed, use only existing project tooling and do not add dependencies or alter tests.
payload.required_real_page_visual_acceptance: Not applicable: this is a non-UI algorithm repair with no page, component, or visual surface.
risks: The research report notes that the visible files do not fully specify finite versus integer endpoint requirements, zero-width validity, or whether empty labels are allowed; validation must follow the established src/windows.js contract and test expectations rather than inventing incompatible restrictions.
Lexicographic ordering must use the project/runtime's ordinary string comparison consistently, and sorting must not mutate caller-owned arrays.
unknowns: Exact malformed-window predicate beyond required start/end/labels fields is not fully specified by the research report.
Whether zero-width windows are valid inputs versus merely non-overlapping intervals is not established by the visible evidence.
Whether empty label arrays or empty label strings are valid is not established by the visible evidence.
blockers: No implementation blocker for planning. The Developer must resolve the noted validation edge semantics from the existing src/windows.js contract and tests while preserving the explicit user requirements.

payload.objective: Repair the existing interval-window aggregation defect by implementing one deterministic algorithm in src/windows.js while preserving the existing InvalidWindowError RangeError contract and leaving all tests and dependencies unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Only src/windows.js is modified; no tests are changed, deleted, skipped, or weakened, and no dependency is added.
Every input window is validated before aggregation; malformed windows are converted to InvalidWindowError, which remains a RangeError with code INVALID_WINDOW.
Input is sorted through a copied representation so caller-owned window order and window objects are not mutated.
Windows merge only when their overlap has positive width; an end equal to the next start remains a separate boundary.
Merged labels are unique strings sorted in lexicographic order.
The real project checker is run as npm test, whose underlying command is node --test, and all tests pass.
payload.root_design_decision: Use a validate-then-copy-sort-then-sweep pipeline: validate every window and its start/end/labels shape before any result is produced; sort copied window records by deterministic interval order; sweep from left to right, merging only when next.start is strictly less than the current end, extending the current end as needed, and accumulating labels in a Set before final lexicographic sorting. Equality at the boundary is deliberately non-overlapping.
owned_modification_surfaces: src/windows.js: InvalidWindowError contract preservation, window validation, copied deterministic ordering, positive-width overlap sweep, and unique lexicographic label aggregation.
ordered_implementation_work: Inspect the existing src/windows.js exports and data shape without changing tests or package configuration.

Implement a validation predicate for every window consistent with the observed start/end/labels object shape; route all malformed cases through InvalidWindowError and preserve RangeError plus code INVALID_WINDOW.
Create a shallow copied working collection (and copied label arrays/records where needed), then sort it deterministically without mutating caller input.

Implement the sweep: start a new output interval when there is no positive-width overlap; merge only when next.start < current.end; keep next.start === current.end separate; extend end to the maximum endpoint.
Finalize each output interval with deduplicated labels sorted by standard lexicographic string ordering, preserving the expected output shape and named exports.
Run npm test through the real project checker and confirm the underlying node --test suite passes; report the exact result.
positive_non_user_interface_verification: Run npm test from the project root (the package script invokes node --test).
Confirm all existing tests pass, including overlap merge, adjacent-boundary separation, and InvalidWindowError RangeError/code assertions.
If implementation-time checks are needed, use only existing project tooling and do not add dependencies or alter tests.
payload.required_real_page_visual_acceptance: Not applicable: this is a non-UI algorithm repair with no page, component, or visual surface.
risks: The research report notes that the visible files do not fully specify finite versus integer endpoint requirements, zero-width validity, or whether empty labels are allowed; validation must follow the established src/windows.js contract and test expectations rather than inventing incompatible restrictions.
Lexicographic ordering must use the project/runtime's ordinary string comparison consistently, and sorting must not mutate caller-owned arrays.
unknowns: Exact malformed-window predicate beyond required start/end/labels fields is not fully specified by the research report.
Whether zero-width windows are valid inputs versus merely non-overlapping intervals is not established by the visible evidence.
Whether empty label arrays or empty label strings are valid is not established by the visible evidence.
blockers: No implementation blocker for planning. The Developer must resolve the noted validation edge semantics from the existing src/windows.js contract and tests while preserving the explicit user requirements.

payload.objective: Repair the existing interval-window aggregation defect by implementing one deterministic algorithm in src/windows.js while preserving the existing InvalidWindowError RangeError contract and leaving all tests and dependencies unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Only src/windows.js is modified; no tests are changed, deleted, skipped, or weakened, and no dependency is added.
Every input window is validated before aggregation; malformed windows are converted to InvalidWindowError, which remains a RangeError with code INVALID_WINDOW.
Input is sorted through a copied representation so caller-owned window order and window objects are not mutated.
Windows merge only when their overlap has positive width; an end equal to the next start remains a separate boundary.
Merged labels are unique strings sorted in lexicographic order.
The real project checker is run as npm test, whose underlying command is node --test, and all tests pass.
payload.root_design_decision: Use a validate-then-copy-sort-then-sweep pipeline: validate every window and its start/end/labels shape before any result is produced; sort copied window records by deterministic interval order; sweep from left to right, merging only when next.start is strictly less than the current end, extending the current end as needed, and accumulating labels in a Set before final lexicographic sorting. Equality at the boundary is deliberately non-overlapping.
owned_modification_surfaces: src/windows.js: InvalidWindowError contract preservation, window validation, copied deterministic ordering, positive-width overlap sweep, and unique lexicographic label aggregation.
ordered_implementation_work: Inspect the existing src/windows.js exports and data shape without changing tests or package configuration.

Implement a validation predicate for every window consistent with the observed start/end/labels object shape; route all malformed cases through InvalidWindowError and preserve RangeError plus code INVALID_WINDOW.
Create a shallow copied working collection (and copied label arrays/records where needed), then sort it deterministically without mutating caller input.

Implement the sweep: start a new output interval when there is no positive-width overlap; merge only when next.start < current.end; keep next.start === current.end separate; extend end to the maximum endpoint.
Finalize each output interval with deduplicated labels sorted by standard lexicographic string ordering, preserving the expected output shape and named exports.
Run npm test through the real project checker and confirm the underlying node --test suite passes; report the exact result.
positive_non_user_interface_verification: Run npm test from the project root (the package script invokes node --test).
Confirm all existing tests pass, including overlap merge, adjacent-boundary separation, and InvalidWindowError RangeError/code assertions.
If implementation-time checks are needed, use only existing project tooling and do not add dependencies or alter tests.
payload.required_real_page_visual_acceptance: Not applicable: this is a non-UI algorithm repair with no page, component, or visual surface.
risks: The research report notes that the visible files do not fully specify finite versus integer endpoint requirements, zero-width validity, or whether empty labels are allowed; validation must follow the established src/windows.js contract and test expectations rather than inventing incompatible restrictions.
Lexicographic ordering must use the project/runtime's ordinary string comparison consistently, and sorting must not mutate caller-owned arrays.
unknowns: Exact malformed-window predicate beyond required start/end/labels fields is not fully specified by the research report.
Whether zero-width windows are valid inputs versus merely non-overlapping intervals is not established by the visible evidence.
Whether empty label arrays or empty label strings are valid is not established by the visible evidence.
blockers: No implementation blocker for planning. The Developer must resolve the noted validation edge semantics from the existing src/windows.js contract and tests while preserving the explicit user requirements.

payload.objective: Repair the existing interval-window aggregation defect by implementing one deterministic algorithm in src/windows.js while preserving the existing InvalidWindowError RangeError contract and leaving all tests and dependencies unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Only src/windows.js is modified; no tests are changed, deleted, skipped, or weakened, and no dependency is added.
Every input window is validated before aggregation; malformed windows are converted to InvalidWindowError, which remains a RangeError with code INVALID_WINDOW.
Input is sorted through a copied representation so caller-owned window order and window objects are not mutated.
Windows merge only when their overlap has positive width; an end equal to the next start remains a separate boundary.
Merged labels are unique strings sorted in lexicographic order.
The real project checker is run as npm test, whose underlying command is node --test, and all tests pass.
payload.root_design_decision: Use a validate-then-copy-sort-then-sweep pipeline: validate every window and its start/end/labels shape before any result is produced; sort copied window records by deterministic interval order; sweep from left to right, merging only when next.start is strictly less than the current end, extending the current end as needed, and accumulating labels in a Set before final lexicographic sorting. Equality at the boundary is deliberately non-overlapping.
owned_modification_surfaces: src/windows.js: InvalidWindowError contract preservation, window validation, copied deterministic ordering, positive-width overlap sweep, and unique lexicographic label aggregation.
ordered_implementation_work: Inspect the existing src/windows.js exports and data shape without changing tests or package configuration.

Implement a validation predicate for every window consistent with the observed start/end/labels object shape; route all malformed cases through InvalidWindowError and preserve RangeError plus code INVALID_WINDOW.
Create a shallow copied working collection (and copied label arrays/records where needed), then sort it deterministically without mutating caller input.

Implement the sweep: start a new output interval when there is no positive-width overlap; merge only when next.start < current.end; keep next.start === current.end separate; extend end to the maximum endpoint.
Finalize each output interval with deduplicated labels sorted by standard lexicographic string ordering, preserving the expected output shape and named exports.
Run npm test through the real project checker and confirm the underlying node --test suite passes; report the exact result.
positive_non_user_interface_verification: Run npm test from the project root (the package script invokes node --test).
Confirm all existing tests pass, including overlap merge, adjacent-boundary separation, and InvalidWindowError RangeError/code assertions.
If implementation-time checks are needed, use only existing project tooling and do not add dependencies or alter tests.
payload.required_real_page_visual_acceptance: Not applicable: this is a non-UI algorithm repair with no page, component, or visual surface.
risks: The research report notes that the visible files do not fully specify finite versus integer endpoint requirements, zero-width validity, or whether empty labels are allowed; validation must follow the established src/windows.js contract and test expectations rather than inventing incompatible restrictions.
Lexicographic ordering must use the project/runtime's ordinary string comparison consistently, and sorting must not mutate caller-owned arrays.
unknowns: Exact malformed-window predicate beyond required start/end/labels fields is not fully specified by the research report.
Whether zero-width windows are valid inputs versus merely non-overlapping intervals is not established by the visible evidence.
Whether empty label arrays or empty label strings are valid is not established by the visible evidence.
blockers: No implementation blocker for planning. The Developer must resolve the noted validation edge semantics from the existing src/windows.js contract and tests while preserving the explicit user requirements.

boundaries: Sort a copy without mutating caller input

unknowns: Visible files do not define finite versus integer endpoints.

payload.objective: Repair the existing interval-window aggregation defect by implementing one deterministic algorithm in src/windows.js while preserving the existing InvalidWindowError RangeError contract and leaving all tests and dependencies unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Only src/windows.js is modified; no tests are changed, deleted, skipped, or weakened, and no dependency is added.
Every input window is validated before aggregation; malformed windows are converted to InvalidWindowError, which remains a RangeError with code INVALID_WINDOW.
Input is sorted through a copied representation so caller-owned window order and window objects are not mutated.
Windows merge only when their overlap has positive width; an end equal to the next start remains a separate boundary.
Merged labels are unique strings sorted in lexicographic order.
The real project checker is run as npm test, whose underlying command is node --test, and all tests pass.
payload.root_design_decision: Use a validate-then-copy-sort-then-sweep pipeline: validate every window and its start/end/labels shape before any result is produced; sort copied window records by deterministic interval order; sweep from left to right, merging only when next.start is strictly less than the current end, extending the current end as needed, and accumulating labels in a Set before final lexicographic sorting. Equality at the boundary is deliberately non-overlapping.
owned_modification_surfaces: src/windows.js: InvalidWindowError contract preservation, window validation, copied deterministic ordering, positive-width overlap sweep, and unique lexicographic label aggregation.
ordered_implementation_work: Inspect the existing src/windows.js exports and data shape without changing tests or package configuration.

Implement a validation predicate for every window consistent with the observed start/end/labels object shape; route all malformed cases through InvalidWindowError and preserve RangeError plus code INVALID_WINDOW.
Create a shallow copied working collection (and copied label arrays/records where needed), then sort it deterministically without mutating caller input.

Implement the sweep: start a new output interval when there is no positive-width overlap; merge only when next.start < current.end; keep next.start === current.end separate; extend end to the maximum endpoint.
Finalize each output interval with deduplicated labels sorted by standard lexicographic string ordering, preserving the expected output shape and named exports.
Run npm test through the real project checker and confirm the underlying node --test suite passes; report the exact result.
positive_non_user_interface_verification: Run npm test from the project root (the package script invokes node --test).
Confirm all existing tests pass, including overlap merge, adjacent-boundary separation, and InvalidWindowError RangeError/code assertions.
If implementation-time checks are needed, use only existing project tooling and do not add dependencies or alter tests.
payload.required_real_page_visual_acceptance: Not applicable: this is a non-UI algorithm repair with no page, component, or visual surface.
risks: The research report notes that the visible files do not fully specify finite versus integer endpoint requirements, zero-width validity, or whether empty labels are allowed; validation must follow the established src/windows.js contract and test expectations rather than inventing incompatible restrictions.
Lexicographic ordering must use the project/runtime's ordinary string comparison consistently, and sorting must not mutate caller-owned arrays.
unknowns: Exact malformed-window predicate beyond required start/end/labels fields is not fully specified by the research report.
Whether zero-width windows are valid inputs versus merely non-overlapping intervals is not established by the visible evidence.
Whether empty label arrays or empty label strings are valid is not established by the visible evidence.
blockers: No implementation blocker for planning. The Developer must resolve the noted validation edge semantics from the existing src/windows.js contract and tests while preserving the explicit user requirements.

payload.objective: Repair the existing interval-window aggregation defect by implementing one deterministic algorithm in src/windows.js while preserving the existing InvalidWindowError RangeError contract and leaving all tests and dependencies unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Only src/windows.js is modified; no tests are changed, deleted, skipped, or weakened, and no dependency is added.
Every input window is validated before aggregation; malformed windows are converted to InvalidWindowError, which remains a RangeError with code INVALID_WINDOW.
Input is sorted through a copied representation so caller-owned window order and window objects are not mutated.
Windows merge only when their overlap has positive width; an end equal to the next start remains a separate boundary.
Merged labels are unique strings sorted in lexicographic order.
The real project checker is run as npm test, whose underlying command is node --test, and all tests pass.
payload.root_design_decision: Use a validate-then-copy-sort-then-sweep pipeline: validate every window and its start/end/labels shape before any result is produced; sort copied window records by deterministic interval order; sweep from left to right, merging only when next.start is strictly less than the current end, extending the current end as needed, and accumulating labels in a Set before final lexicographic sorting. Equality at the boundary is deliberately non-overlapping.
owned_modification_surfaces: src/windows.js: InvalidWindowError contract preservation, window validation, copied deterministic ordering, positive-width overlap sweep, and unique lexicographic label aggregation.
ordered_implementation_work: Inspect the existing src/windows.js exports and data shape without changing tests or package configuration.

Implement a validation predicate for every window consistent with the observed start/end/labels object shape; route all malformed cases through InvalidWindowError and preserve RangeError plus code INVALID_WINDOW.
Create a shallow copied working collection (and copied label arrays/records where needed), then sort it deterministically without mutating caller input.

Implement the sweep: start a new output interval when there is no positive-width overlap; merge only when next.start < current.end; keep next.start === current.end separate; extend end to the maximum endpoint.
Finalize each output interval with deduplicated labels sorted by standard lexicographic string ordering, preserving the expected output shape and named exports.
Run npm test through the real project checker and confirm the underlying node --test suite passes; report the exact result.
positive_non_user_interface_verification: Run npm test from the project root (the package script invokes node --test).

payload.objective: Repair the existing interval-window aggregation defect by implementing one deterministic algorithm in src/windows.js while preserving the existing InvalidWindowError RangeError contract and leaving all tests and dependencies unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Only src/windows.js is modified; no tests are changed, deleted, skipped, or weakened, and no dependency is added.
Every input window is validated before aggregation; malformed windows are converted to InvalidWindowError, which remains a RangeError with code INVALID_WINDOW.
Input is sorted through a copied representation so caller-owned window order and window objects are not mutated.
Windows merge only when their overlap has positive width; an end equal to the next start remains a separate boundary.
Merged labels are unique strings sorted in lexicographic order.
The real project checker is run as npm test, whose underlying command is node --test, and all tests pass.
payload.root_design_decision: Use a validate-then-copy-sort-then-sweep pipeline: validate every window and its start/end/labels shape before any result is produced; sort copied window records by deterministic interval order; sweep from left to right, merging only when next.start is strictly less than the current end, extending the current end as needed, and accumulating labels in a Set before final lexicographic sorting. Equality at the boundary is deliberately non-overlapping.
owned_modification_surfaces: src/windows.js: InvalidWindowError contract preservation, window validation, copied deterministic ordering, positive-width overlap sweep, and unique lexicographic label aggregation.
ordered_implementation_work: Inspect the existing src/windows.js exports and data shape without changing tests or package configuration.

Implement a validation predicate for every window consistent with the observed start/end/labels object shape; route all malformed cases through InvalidWindowError and preserve RangeError plus code INVALID_WINDOW.
Create a shallow copied working collection (and copied label arrays/records where needed), then sort it deterministically without mutating caller input.

Implement the sweep: start a new output interval when there is no positive-width overlap; merge only when next.start < current.end; keep next.start === current.end separate; extend end to the maximum endpoint.
Finalize each output interval with deduplicated labels sorted by standard lexicographic string ordering, preserving the expected output shape and named exports.
Run npm test through the real project checker and confirm the underlying node --test suite passes; report the exact result.
positive_non_user_interface_verification: Run npm test from the project root (the package script invokes node --test).
Confirm all existing tests pass, including overlap merge, adjacent-boundary separation, and InvalidWindowError RangeError/code assertions.
If implementation-time checks are needed, use only existing project tooling and do not add dependencies or alter tests.
payload.required_real_page_visual_acceptance: Not applicable: this is a non-UI algorithm repair with no page, component, or visual surface.
risks: The research report notes that the visible files do not fully specify finite versus integer endpoint requirements, zero-width validity, or whether empty labels are allowed; validation must follow the established src/windows.js contract and test expectations rather than inventing incompatible restrictions.
Lexicographic ordering must use the project/runtime's ordinary string comparison consistently, and sorting must not mutate caller-owned arrays.
unknowns: Exact malformed-window predicate beyond required start/end/labels fields is not fully specified by the research report.
Whether zero-width windows are valid inputs versus merely non-overlapping intervals is not established by the visible evidence.
Whether empty label arrays or empty label strings are valid is not established by the visible evidence.
blockers: No implementation blocker for planning. The Developer must resolve the noted validation edge semantics from the existing src/windows.js contract and tests while preserving the explicit user requirements.

payload.objective: Repair the existing interval-window aggregation defect by implementing one deterministic algorithm in src/windows.js while preserving the existing InvalidWindowError RangeError contract and leaving all tests and dependencies unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Only src/windows.js is modified; no tests are changed, deleted, skipped, or weakened, and no dependency is added.
Every input window is validated before aggregation; malformed windows are converted to InvalidWindowError, which remains a RangeError with code INVALID_WINDOW.
Input is sorted through a copied representation so caller-owned window order and window objects are not mutated.
Windows merge only when their overlap has positive width; an end equal to the next start remains a separate boundary.
Merged labels are unique strings sorted in lexicographic order.
The real project checker is run as npm test, whose underlying command is node --test, and all tests pass.
payload.root_design_decision: Use a validate-then-copy-sort-then-sweep pipeline: validate every window and its start/end/labels shape before any result is produced; sort copied window records by deterministic interval order; sweep from left to right, merging only when next.start is strictly less than the current end, extending the current end as needed, and accumulating labels in a Set before final lexicographic sorting. Equality at the boundary is deliberately non-overlapping.
owned_modification_surfaces: src/windows.js: InvalidWindowError contract preservation, window validation, copied deterministic ordering, positive-width overlap sweep, and unique lexicographic label aggregation.
ordered_implementation_work: Inspect the existing src/windows.js exports and data shape without changing tests or package configuration.

Implement a validation predicate for every window consistent with the observed start/end/labels object shape; route all malformed cases through InvalidWindowError and preserve RangeError plus code INVALID_WINDOW.
Create a shallow copied working collection (and copied label arrays/records where needed), then sort it deterministically without mutating caller input.

Implement the sweep: start a new output interval when there is no positive-width overlap; merge only when next.start < current.end; keep next.start === current.end separate; extend end to the maximum endpoint.
Finalize each output interval with deduplicated labels sorted by standard lexicographic string ordering, preserving the expected output shape and named exports.
Run npm test through the real project checker and confirm the underlying node --test suite passes; report the exact result.
positive_non_user_interface_verification: Run npm test from the project root (the package script invokes node --test).
Confirm all existing tests pass, including overlap merge, adjacent-boundary separation, and InvalidWindowError RangeError/code assertions.
If implementation-time checks are needed, use only existing project tooling and do not add dependencies or alter tests.
payload.required_real_page_visual_acceptance: Not applicable: this is a non-UI algorithm repair with no page, component, or visual surface.
risks: The research report notes that the visible files do not fully specify finite versus integer endpoint requirements, zero-width validity, or whether empty labels are allowed; validation must follow the established src/windows.js contract and test expectations rather than inventing incompatible restrictions.
Lexicographic ordering must use the project/runtime's ordinary string comparison consistently, and sorting must not mutate caller-owned arrays.
unknowns: Exact malformed-window predicate beyond required start/end/labels fields is not fully specified by the research report.
Whether zero-width windows are valid inputs versus merely non-overlapping intervals is not established by the visible evidence.
Whether empty label arrays or empty label strings are valid is not established by the visible evidence.
blockers: No implementation blocker for planning. The Developer must resolve the noted validation edge semantics from the existing src/windows.js contract and tests while preserving the explicit user requirements.

payload.objective: Repair the existing interval-window aggregation defect by implementing one deterministic algorithm in src/windows.js while preserving the existing InvalidWindowError RangeError contract and leaving all tests and dependencies unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Only src/windows.js is modified; no tests are changed, deleted, skipped, or weakened, and no dependency is added.
Every input window is validated before aggregation; malformed windows are converted to InvalidWindowError, which remains a RangeError with code INVALID_WINDOW.
Input is sorted through a copied representation so caller-owned window order and window objects are not mutated.
Windows merge only when their overlap has positive width; an end equal to the next start remains a separate boundary.
Merged labels are unique strings sorted in lexicographic order.
The real project checker is run as npm test, whose underlying command is node --test, and all tests pass.
payload.root_design_decision: Use a validate-then-copy-sort-then-sweep pipeline: validate every window and its start/end/labels shape before any result is produced; sort copied window records by deterministic interval order; sweep from left to right, merging only when next.start is strictly less than the current end, extending the current end as needed, and accumulating labels in a Set before final lexicographic sorting. Equality at the boundary is deliberately non-overlapping.
owned_modification_surfaces: src/windows.js: InvalidWindowError contract preservation, window validation, copied deterministic ordering, positive-width overlap sweep, and unique lexicographic label aggregation.
ordered_implementation_work: Inspect the existing src/windows.js exports and data shape without changing tests or package configuration.

Implement a validation predicate for every window consistent with the observed start/end/labels object shape; route all malformed cases through InvalidWindowError and preserve RangeError plus code INVALID_WINDOW.
Create a shallow copied working collection (and copied label arrays/records where needed), then sort it deterministically without mutating caller input.

Implement the sweep: start a new output interval when there is no positive-width overlap; merge only when next.start < current.end; keep next.start === current.end separate; extend end to the maximum endpoint.
Finalize each output interval with deduplicated labels sorted by standard lexicographic string ordering, preserving the expected output shape and named exports.
Run npm test through the real project checker and confirm the underlying node --test suite passes; report the exact result.
positive_non_user_interface_verification: Run npm test from the project root (the package script invokes node --test).
Confirm all existing tests pass, including overlap merge, adjacent-boundary separation, and InvalidWindowError RangeError/code assertions.
If implementation-time checks are needed, use only existing project tooling and do not add dependencies or alter tests.
payload.required_real_page_visual_acceptance: Not applicable: this is a non-UI algorithm repair with no page, component, or visual surface.
risks: The research report notes that the visible files do not fully specify finite versus integer endpoint requirements, zero-width validity, or whether empty labels are allowed; validation must follow the established src/windows.js contract and test expectations rather than inventing incompatible restrictions.
Lexicographic ordering must use the project/runtime's ordinary string comparison consistently, and sorting must not mutate caller-owned arrays.
unknowns: Exact malformed-window predicate beyond required start/end/labels fields is not fully specified by the research report.
Whether zero-width windows are valid inputs versus merely non-overlapping intervals is not established by the visible evidence.
Whether empty label arrays or empty label strings are valid is not established by the visible evidence.
blockers: No implementation blocker for planning. The Developer must resolve the noted validation edge semantics from the existing src/windows.js contract and tests while preserving the explicit user requirements.

payload.objective: Repair the existing interval-window aggregation defect by implementing one deterministic algorithm in src/windows.js while preserving the existing InvalidWindowError RangeError contract and leaving all tests and dependencies unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Only src/windows.js is modified; no tests are changed, deleted, skipped, or weakened, and no dependency is added.
Every input window is validated before aggregation; malformed windows are converted to InvalidWindowError, which remains a RangeError with code INVALID_WINDOW.
Input is sorted through a copied representation so caller-owned window order and window objects are not mutated.
Windows merge only when their overlap has positive width; an end equal to the next start remains a separate boundary.
Merged labels are unique strings sorted in lexicographic order.
The real project checker is run as npm test, whose underlying command is node --test, and all tests pass.
payload.root_design_decision: Use a validate-then-copy-sort-then-sweep pipeline: validate every window and its start/end/labels shape before any result is produced; sort copied window records by deterministic interval order; sweep from left to right, merging only when next.start is strictly less than the current end, extending the current end as needed, and accumulating labels in a Set before final lexicographic sorting. Equality at the boundary is deliberately non-overlapping.
owned_modification_surfaces: src/windows.js: InvalidWindowError contract preservation, window validation, copied deterministic ordering, positive-width overlap sweep, and unique lexicographic label aggregation.
ordered_implementation_work: Inspect the existing src/windows.js exports and data shape without changing tests or package configuration.

Implement a validation predicate for every window consistent with the observed start/end/labels object shape; route all malformed cases through InvalidWindowError and preserve RangeError plus code INVALID_WINDOW.
Create a shallow copied working collection (and copied label arrays/records where needed), then sort it deterministically without mutating caller input.

Implement the sweep: start a new output interval when there is no positive-width overlap; merge only when next.start < current.end; keep next.start === current.end separate; extend end to the maximum endpoint.
Finalize each output interval with deduplicated labels sorted by standard lexicographic string ordering, preserving the expected output shape and named exports.
Run npm test through the real project checker and confirm the underlying node --test suite passes; report the exact result.
positive_non_user_interface_verification: Run npm test from the project root (the package script invokes node --test).
Confirm all existing tests pass, including overlap merge, adjacent-boundary separation, and InvalidWindowError RangeError/code assertions.
If implementation-time checks are needed, use only existing project tooling and do not add dependencies or alter tests.
payload.required_real_page_visual_acceptance: Not applicable: this is a non-UI algorithm repair with no page, component, or visual surface.
risks: The research report notes that the visible files do not fully specify finite versus integer endpoint requirements, zero-width validity, or whether empty labels are allowed; validation must follow the established src/windows.js contract and test expectations rather than inventing incompatible restrictions.
Lexicographic ordering must use the project/runtime's ordinary string comparison consistently, and sorting must not mutate caller-owned arrays.
unknowns: Exact malformed-window predicate beyond required start/end/labels fields is not fully specified by the research report.
Whether zero-width windows are valid inputs versus merely non-overlapping intervals is not established by the visible evidence.
Whether empty label arrays or empty label strings are valid is not established by the visible evidence.
blockers: No implementation blocker for planning. The Developer must resolve the noted validation edge semantics from the existing src/windows.js contract and tests while preserving the explicit user requirements.

payload.objective: Repair the existing interval-window aggregation defect by implementing one deterministic algorithm in src/windows.js while preserving the existing InvalidWindowError RangeError contract and leaving all tests and dependencies unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Only src/windows.js is modified; no tests are changed, deleted, skipped, or weakened, and no dependency is added.
Every input window is validated before aggregation; malformed windows are converted to InvalidWindowError, which remains a RangeError with code INVALID_WINDOW.
Input is sorted through a copied representation so caller-owned window order and window objects are not mutated.
Windows merge only when their overlap has positive width; an end equal to the next start remains a separate boundary.
Merged labels are unique strings sorted in lexicographic order.
The real project checker is run as npm test, whose underlying command is node --test, and all tests pass.
payload.root_design_decision: Use a validate-then-copy-sort-then-sweep pipeline: validate every window and its start/end/labels shape before any result is produced; sort copied window records by deterministic interval order; sweep from left to right, merging only when next.start is strictly less than the current end, extending the current end as needed, and accumulating labels in a Set before final lexicographic sorting. Equality at the boundary is deliberately non-overlapping.
owned_modification_surfaces: src/windows.js: InvalidWindowError contract preservation, window validation, copied deterministic ordering, positive-width overlap sweep, and unique lexicographic label aggregation.
ordered_implementation_work: Inspect the existing src/windows.js exports and data shape without changing tests or package configuration.

Implement a validation predicate for every window consistent with the observed start/end/labels object shape; route all malformed cases through InvalidWindowError and preserve RangeError plus code INVALID_WINDOW.
Create a shallow copied working collection (and copied label arrays/records where needed), then sort it deterministically without mutating caller input.

Implement the sweep: start a new output interval when there is no positive-width overlap; merge only when next.start < current.end; keep next.start === current.end separate; extend end to the maximum endpoint.
Finalize each output interval with deduplicated labels sorted by standard lexicographic string ordering, preserving the expected output shape and named exports.
Run npm test through the real project checker and confirm the underlying node --test suite passes; report the exact result.
positive_non_user_interface_verification: Run npm test from the project root (the package script invokes node --test).
Confirm all existing tests pass, including overlap merge, adjacent-boundary separation, and InvalidWindowError RangeError/code assertions.
If implementation-time checks are needed, use only existing project tooling and do not add dependencies or alter tests.
payload.required_real_page_visual_acceptance: Not applicable: this is a non-UI algorithm repair with no page, component, or visual surface.
risks: The research report notes that the visible files do not fully specify finite versus integer endpoint requirements, zero-width validity, or whether empty labels are allowed; validation must follow the established src/windows.js contract and test expectations rather than inventing incompatible restrictions.
Lexicographic ordering must use the project/runtime's ordinary string comparison consistently, and sorting must not mutate caller-owned arrays.
unknowns: Exact malformed-window predicate beyond required start/end/labels fields is not fully specified by the research report.
Whether zero-width windows are valid inputs versus merely non-overlapping intervals is not established by the visible evidence.
Whether empty label arrays or empty label strings are valid is not established by the visible evidence.
blockers: No implementation blocker for planning. The Developer must resolve the noted validation edge semantics from the existing src/windows.js contract and tests while preserving the explicit user requirements.

payload.objective: Repair the existing interval-window aggregation defect by implementing one deterministic algorithm in src/windows.js while preserving the existing InvalidWindowError RangeError contract and leaving all tests and dependencies unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Only src/windows.js is modified; no tests are changed, deleted, skipped, or weakened, and no dependency is added.
Every input window is validated before aggregation; malformed windows are converted to InvalidWindowError, which remains a RangeError with code INVALID_WINDOW.
Input is sorted through a copied representation so caller-owned window order and window objects are not mutated.
Windows merge only when their overlap has positive width; an end equal to the next start remains a separate boundary.
Merged labels are unique strings sorted in lexicographic order.
The real project checker is run as npm test, whose underlying command is node --test, and all tests pass.
payload.root_design_decision: Use a validate-then-copy-sort-then-sweep pipeline: validate every window and its start/end/labels shape before any result is produced; sort copied window records by deterministic interval order; sweep from left to right, merging only when next.start is strictly less than the current end, extending the current end as needed, and accumulating labels in a Set before final lexicographic sorting. Equality at the boundary is deliberately non-overlapping.
owned_modification_surfaces: src/windows.js: InvalidWindowError contract preservation, window validation, copied deterministic ordering, positive-width overlap sweep, and unique lexicographic label aggregation.
ordered_implementation_work: Inspect the existing src/windows.js exports and data shape without changing tests or package configuration.

Implement a validation predicate for every window consistent with the observed start/end/labels object shape; route all malformed cases through InvalidWindowError and preserve RangeError plus code INVALID_WINDOW.
Create a shallow copied working collection (and copied label arrays/records where needed), then sort it deterministically without mutating caller input.

Implement the sweep: start a new output interval when there is no positive-width overlap; merge only when next.start < current.end; keep next.start === current.end separate; extend end to the maximum endpoint.
Finalize each output interval with deduplicated labels sorted by standard lexicographic string ordering, preserving the expected output shape and named exports.
Run npm test through the real project checker and confirm the underlying node --test suite passes; report the exact result.
positive_non_user_interface_verification: Run npm test from the project root (the package script invokes node --test).
Confirm all existing tests pass, including overlap merge, adjacent-boundary separation, and InvalidWindowError RangeError/code assertions.
If implementation-time checks are needed, use only existing project tooling and do not add dependencies or alter tests.
payload.required_real_page_visual_acceptance: Not applicable: this is a non-UI algorithm repair with no page, component, or visual surface.
risks: The research report notes that the visible files do not fully specify finite versus integer endpoint requirements, zero-width validity, or whether empty labels are allowed; validation must follow the established src/windows.js contract and test expectations rather than inventing incompatible restrictions.
Lexicographic ordering must use the project/runtime's ordinary string comparison consistently, and sorting must not mutate caller-owned arrays.
unknowns: Exact malformed-window predicate beyond required start/end/labels fields is not fully specified by the research report.
Whether zero-width windows are valid inputs versus merely non-overlapping intervals is not established by the visible evidence.
Whether empty label arrays or empty label strings are valid is not established by the visible evidence.
blockers: No implementation blocker for planning. The Developer must resolve the noted validation edge semantics from the existing src/windows.js contract and tests while preserving the explicit user requirements.

payload.objective: Repair the existing interval-window aggregation defect by implementing one deterministic algorithm in src/windows.js while preserving the existing InvalidWindowError RangeError contract and leaving all tests and dependencies unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Only src/windows.js is modified; no tests are changed, deleted, skipped, or weakened, and no dependency is added.
Every input window is validated before aggregation; malformed windows are converted to InvalidWindowError, which remains a RangeError with code INVALID_WINDOW.
Input is sorted through a copied representation so caller-owned window order and window objects are not mutated.
Windows merge only when their overlap has positive width; an end equal to the next start remains a separate boundary.
Merged labels are unique strings sorted in lexicographic order.
The real project checker is run as npm test, whose underlying command is node --test, and all tests pass.
payload.root_design_decision: Use a validate-then-copy-sort-then-sweep pipeline: validate every window and its start/end/labels shape before any result is produced; sort copied window records by deterministic interval order; sweep from left to right, merging only when next.start is strictly less than the current end, extending the current end as needed, and accumulating labels in a Set before final lexicographic sorting. Equality at the boundary is deliberately non-overlapping.
owned_modification_surfaces: src/windows.js: InvalidWindowError contract preservation, window validation, copied deterministic ordering, positive-width overlap sweep, and unique lexicographic label aggregation.
ordered_implementation_work: Inspect the existing src/windows.js exports and data shape without changing tests or package configuration.

Implement a validation predicate for every window consistent with the observed start/end/labels object shape; route all malformed cases through InvalidWindowError and preserve RangeError plus code INVALID_WINDOW.
Create a shallow copied working collection (and copied label arrays/records where needed), then sort it deterministically without mutating caller input.

Implement the sweep: start a new output interval when there is no positive-width overlap; merge only when next.start < current.end; keep next.start === current.end separate; extend end to the maximum endpoint.
Finalize each output interval with deduplicated labels sorted by standard lexicographic string ordering, preserving the expected output shape and named exports.
Run npm test through the real project checker and confirm the underlying node --test suite passes; report the exact result.
positive_non_user_interface_verification: Run npm test from the project root (the package script invokes node --test).
Confirm all existing tests pass, including overlap merge, adjacent-boundary separation, and InvalidWindowError RangeError/code assertions.
If implementation-time checks are needed, use only existing project tooling and do not add dependencies or alter tests.
payload.required_real_page_visual_acceptance: Not applicable: this is a non-UI algorithm repair with no page, component, or visual surface.
risks: The research report notes that the visible files do not fully specify finite versus integer endpoint requirements, zero-width validity, or whether empty labels are allowed; validation must follow the established src/windows.js contract and test expectations rather than inventing incompatible restrictions.
Lexicographic ordering must use the project/runtime's ordinary string comparison consistently, and sorting must not mutate caller-owned arrays.
unknowns: Exact malformed-window predicate beyond required start/end/labels fields is not fully specified by the research report.
Whether zero-width windows are valid inputs versus merely non-overlapping intervals is not established by the visible evidence.
Whether empty label arrays or empty label strings are valid is not established by the visible evidence.
blockers: No implementation blocker for planning. The Developer must resolve the noted validation edge semantics from the existing src/windows.js contract and tests while preserving the explicit user requirements.

payload.objective: Repair the existing interval-window aggregation defect by implementing one deterministic algorithm in src/windows.js while preserving the existing InvalidWindowError RangeError contract and leaving all tests and dependencies unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Only src/windows.js is modified; no tests are changed, deleted, skipped, or weakened, and no dependency is added.
Every input window is validated before aggregation; malformed windows are converted to InvalidWindowError, which remains a RangeError with code INVALID_WINDOW.
Input is sorted through a copied representation so caller-owned window order and window objects are not mutated.
Windows merge only when their overlap has positive width; an end equal to the next start remains a separate boundary.
Merged labels are unique strings sorted in lexicographic order.
The real project checker is run as npm test, whose underlying command is node --test, and all tests pass.
payload.root_design_decision: Use a validate-then-copy-sort-then-sweep pipeline: validate every window and its start/end/labels shape before any result is produced; sort copied window records by deterministic interval order; sweep from left to right, merging only when next.start is strictly less than the current end, extending the current end as needed, and accumulating labels in a Set before final lexicographic sorting. Equality at the boundary is deliberately non-overlapping.
owned_modification_surfaces: src/windows.js: InvalidWindowError contract preservation, window validation, copied deterministic ordering, positive-width overlap sweep, and unique lexicographic label aggregation.
ordered_implementation_work: Inspect the existing src/windows.js exports and data shape without changing tests or package configuration.

Implement a validation predicate for every window consistent with the observed start/end/labels object shape; route all malformed cases through InvalidWindowError and preserve RangeError plus code INVALID_WINDOW.
Create a shallow copied working collection (and copied label arrays/records where needed), then sort it deterministically without mutating caller input.

Implement the sweep: start a new output interval when there is no positive-width overlap; merge only when next.start < current.end; keep next.start === current.end separate; extend end to the maximum endpoint.
Finalize each output interval with deduplicated labels sorted by standard lexicographic string ordering, preserving the expected output shape and named exports.
Run npm test through the real project checker and confirm the underlying node --test suite passes; report the exact result.
positive_non_user_interface_verification: Run npm test from the project root (the package script invokes node --test).
Confirm all existing tests pass, including overlap merge, adjacent-boundary separation, and InvalidWindowError RangeError/code assertions.
If implementation-time checks are needed, use only existing project tooling and do not add dependencies or alter tests.
payload.required_real_page_visual_acceptance: Not applicable: this is a non-UI algorithm repair with no page, component, or visual surface.
risks: The research report notes that the visible files do not fully specify finite versus integer endpoint requirements, zero-width validity, or whether empty labels are allowed; validation must follow the established src/windows.js contract and test expectations rather than inventing incompatible restrictions.
Lexicographic ordering must use the project/runtime's ordinary string comparison consistently, and sorting must not mutate caller-owned arrays.
unknowns: Exact malformed-window predicate beyond required start/end/labels fields is not fully specified by the research report.
Whether zero-width windows are valid inputs versus merely non-overlapping intervals is not established by the visible evidence.
Whether empty label arrays or empty label strings are valid is not established by the visible evidence.
blockers: No implementation blocker for planning. The Developer must resolve the noted validation edge semantics from the existing src/windows.js contract and tests while preserving the explicit user requirements.

payload.objective: Repair the existing interval-window aggregation defect by implementing one deterministic algorithm in src/windows.js while preserving the existing InvalidWindowError RangeError contract and leaving all tests and dependencies unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Only src/windows.js is modified; no tests are changed, deleted, skipped, or weakened, and no dependency is added.
Every input window is validated before aggregation; malformed windows are converted to InvalidWindowError, which remains a RangeError with code INVALID_WINDOW.
Input is sorted through a copied representation so caller-owned window order and window objects are not mutated.
Windows merge only when their overlap has positive width; an end equal to the next start remains a separate boundary.
Merged labels are unique strings sorted in lexicographic order.
The real project checker is run as npm test, whose underlying command is node --test, and all tests pass.
payload.root_design_decision: Use a validate-then-copy-sort-then-sweep pipeline: validate every window and its start/end/labels shape before any result is produced; sort copied window records by deterministic interval order; sweep from left to right, merging only when next.start is strictly less than the current end, extending the current end as needed, and accumulating labels in a Set before final lexicographic sorting. Equality at the boundary is deliberately non-overlapping.
owned_modification_surfaces: src/windows.js: InvalidWindowError contract preservation, window validation, copied deterministic ordering, positive-width overlap sweep, and unique lexicographic label aggregation.
ordered_implementation_work: Inspect the existing src/windows.js exports and data shape without changing tests or package configuration.

Implement a validation predicate for every window consistent with the observed start/end/labels object shape; route all malformed cases through InvalidWindowError and preserve RangeError plus code INVALID_WINDOW.
Create a shallow copied working collection (and copied label arrays/records where needed), then sort it deterministically without mutating caller input.

Implement the sweep: start a new output interval when there is no positive-width overlap; merge only when next.start < current.end; keep next.start === current.end separate; extend end to the maximum endpoint.
Finalize each output interval with deduplicated labels sorted by standard lexicographic string ordering, preserving the expected output shape and named exports.
Run npm test through the real project checker and confirm the underlying node --test suite passes; report the exact result.
positive_non_user_interface_verification: Run npm test from the project root (the package script invokes node --test).
Confirm all existing tests pass, including overlap merge, adjacent-boundary separation, and InvalidWindowError RangeError/code assertions.
If implementation-time checks are needed, use only existing project tooling and do not add dependencies or alter tests.
payload.required_real_page_visual_acceptance: Not applicable: this is a non-UI algorithm repair with no page, component, or visual surface.
risks: The research report notes that the visible files do not fully specify finite versus integer endpoint requirements, zero-width validity, or whether empty labels are allowed; validation must follow the established src/windows.js contract and test expectations rather than inventing incompatible restrictions.
Lexicographic ordering must use the project/runtime's ordinary string comparison consistently, and sorting must not mutate caller-owned arrays.
unknowns: Exact malformed-window predicate beyond required start/end/labels fields is not fully specified by the research report.
Whether zero-width windows are valid inputs versus merely non-overlapping intervals is not established by the visible evidence.
Whether empty label arrays or empty label strings are valid is not established by the visible evidence.
blockers: No implementation blocker for planning. The Developer must resolve the noted validation edge semantics from the existing src/windows.js contract and tests while preserving the explicit user requirements.
